DDoS Attack on Public Endpoints [Denial of Service, CWE-400] on CloudFront Distribution, Application Load Balancer, API Gateway: Attackers can generate massive amounts of traffic targeting the public endpoints, potentially exhausting resources and preventing legitimate users from accessing the service. A botnet could be used to generate thousands of requests per second to the ALB or API Gateway endpoints, overwhelming the system's capacity to handle legitimate traffic.

Single Point of Failure in Load Balancer Configuration [Denial of Service, CWE-710] on Application Load Balancer, ECS Services: If the ALB experiences issues or becomes overwhelmed, all incoming traffic would be affected as there's no redundancy in the load balancing layer. A targeted attack or technical failure affecting the ALB could disrupt all incoming traffic to the application, even if the backend services remain healthy.

Insecure Service-to-Service Communication [Spoofing, Information Disclosure, Tampering, CWE-319] on User Service, Content Service, Social Service, Notification Service: Without a service mesh, services communicate directly over the network without enforced encryption or strong mutual authentication, potentially allowing unauthorized access or eavesdropping. Inefficient Database Connection Management [Denial of Service, CWE-404] on Aurora PostgreSQL, User Service, Content Service: Each service instance creates its own database connections without pooling, potentially exhausting database connection limits during high load or attack scenarios. An attacker could trigger multiple rapid requests causing services to create many database connections, exhausting the connection pool and causing service disruption.

Exposed AWS Service Endpoints [Information Disclosure, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-284] on S3, DynamoDB, CloudWatch, Secrets Manager, ECS Services: Services accessing AWS APIs through public endpoints expose traffic to potential interception and make the system vulnerable to credential theft and unauthorized access. Insufficient Secrets Management [Information Disclosure, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-798] on ECS Services, Aurora PostgreSQL, Redis, MSK, OpenSearch: Sensitive credentials and configuration values might be exposed through environment variables or configuration files rather than being properly managed through Secrets Manager. An attacker who gains access to the ECS task definitions or environment variables could potentially extract sensitive credentials.
